skills.connect.p1: Claude Code speaks MCP natively. Register this Station under the name monkeyllm and put the paired key in the header — from then on the forest's tools are in every session.
skills.connect.sub: One command registers the MCP server; the tools arrive by themselves.
skills.connect.title: Step 2 — point Claude Code at this Station
skills.install.english: The file's body is English on purpose: it addresses the model, not you — like SQL and node ids, it is content the console does not rewrite.
skills.install.or_files: Or save them by hand — this is every file the script writes:
skills.install.p1: One paste writes the whole skill where your agent will look for it. From then on, questions in these forests' domain make it recall from them first — and offer to save what it learns.
skills.install.sub: Generated for this exact Station and these forests, delivered by your browser.
skills.install.title: Step 4 — hand your agent the skill
skills.locked: The Skills console teaches an AI to read this forest, and your key cannot read here.
skills.other.manual: The full surface — every tool, every route, every deployment knob — is documented in MCP / API / Integrations, for whoever administers this Station.
skills.other.p1: Nothing above is particular to Claude Code beyond the install path. Register the endpoint below wherever your runtime configures MCP servers, and hand it the same instructions.
skills.other.sub: The same endpoint, the same key, any MCP-capable runtime.
skills.other.title: Any other agent
skills.pair.once: The key is shown once, in the reply. It expires on its own; an administrator can revoke it in Access at any time.
skills.pair.p1: Your agent needs a credential that is yours, not an administrator's to mint: pairing derives one from your password, carrying your own access narrowed to reading and feeding. Swap in your own username and password; the reply is the key.
skills.pair.sub: Pairing turns your password into a key that can only narrow, never add.
skills.pair.title: Step 1 — pair a key of your own
skills.shape.blocks_hint: Each block is a separate file. What the agent never reads never costs it anything.
skills.shape.core_cost: tokens in the core — what a session pays when the skill fires
skills.shape.folder_note: A folder is the shape Claude Code and its kin expect, and the one that keeps the references out of the context window until they are wanted.
skills.shape.multi_hint: More than one forest bakes a routing table — which forest holds what — read from coverage as the file is generated.
skills.shape.one_hint: The skill teaches forests() as its first call, so a lapsed grant reads as a narrowed key, never as a broken skill.
skills.shape.p1: The core teaches recall and is a complete skill on its own; everything else ships as a reference file the agent reads only when it needs it. Blocks start selected to match what your key can do here — widen them if you are preparing this for somebody whose key is wider.
skills.shape.refs_cost: more across {n} reference(s), read on demand
skills.shape.single_cost: tokens, all of it loaded whenever the skill fires
skills.shape.single_note: One file for runtimes that take no folder. Same instructions as the folder, inlined — and all of them loaded every time.
skills.shape.sub: A skill your agent loads whole, so it should hold what that agent actually does.
skills.shape.title: Step 3 — size the skill to the agent
skills.what.p1: Everything this console shows — the tree, the answers, the datasets — is also reachable by your own AI, through MCP. The skill below teaches it the habit: recall from this forest before answering, save what is worth keeping, cite the nodes it read. Installed once, every conversation starts with this forest's knowledge behind it.
skills.what.p2: Four steps: pair a key of your own, point your agent at this Station, choose how much skill it needs, hand it the files. Every snippet on this page already carries this Station's address and the forests you picked — nothing to edit, nothing to guess.
skills.what.sub: A skill is a small instruction file your agent loads. This one teaches it to remember here.
skills.what.title: Your AI, with this forest for a memory
